newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Higher imported inflation boosts S.African Feb PPI.
newsitem.headline: Higher imported inflation boosts S.African Feb PPI.

text.p: Imported inflation was the main contributor to the 0.4 percent month-on-month rise in the producer price index in February, the Central Statistical Service said on Thursday.
PPI grew 0.4 percent month-on-month and 9.3 percent year-on-year in February compared with 0.4 percent and 9.2 percent increases in January.
A Reuters consensus poll of economists had called for a 0.7 and 9.5 percent rise.

CSS said the imported component of producer inflation grew one percent month-on-month and 10.3 percent year-on-year, while the local component was up 0.4 percent month-on-month and 9.2 percent from February a year ago.

The service said the "substantial" increase in imported prices came on the back of a 3.2 percent month-on-month increase in mining and quarrying product prices and 2.3 percent growth in chemicals and chemical product prices.
Other price increases were recorded in the beverages and wood and wood products sectors, which both grew 0.5 percent, while paper, paper products and printing prices rose 0.2 percent.
At the same time, imported prices for agricultural food eased 5.1 percent, while other agricultural product prices fell 1.3 percent.
Among locally produced commodities, non-metallic and mineral product prices and mining and quarrying product prices showed the largest month-on-month gains, rising 3.7 and 3.0 percent respectively.
Other large price increases were recorded by the electricity, up 2.3 percent, electrical machinery and apparatus, which grew 1.5 percent and a 1.2 percent contribution from the transport sector.
